messages.author: 7e01d2d073ea9e7e
messages.subject: neighborhood graph with unconnected regions
parts:
Dear list,

I am running a Poisson model including a BYM latent Gaussian field. My neighborhood graph consists of different larger regions where only the areas within a specific region are connected but not the individual regions themselves. This results in the following warning: "graph for the model bym has XXX connected components!!! Model is revised accordingly." In which sense is the model revised? Should I and, if so, how can I account for the fact of non-connected regions?

Any hint is appreciated.

Best,
Marco

messages.author: b453c29749de564d
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] neighborhood graph with unconnected regions
parts:
On Fri, 2016-07-15 at 05:24 -0700, Marco Helbich wrote:
> Dear list,
>
> I am running a Poisson model including a BYM latent Gaussian field.
> My neighborhood graph consists of different larger regions where only
> the areas within a specific region are connected but not the
> individual regions themselves. This results in the following warning:
> "graph for the model bym has XXX connected components!!! Model is
> revised accordingly." In which sense is the model revised? Should I
> and, if so, how can I account for the fact of non-connected regions?
>

If the option adjust.for.con.comp=TRUE (default) then the model is
adjusted if the graph has more than one connected compoment. This
adjustment can be disabled setting this option to FALSE. If
adjust.for.con.comp=TRUE then constr=TRUE is interpreted as a sum-to-
zero constraint on EACH connected component in the graph and the
rankdef parameter is set to the number of connected components.


see inla.doc("besag")

Best
H
